issues: Subject clarity failed: intake does not define one clear manufactured object.
Abstract drift risk is elevated: intake does not sufficiently lock object-first behavior.
fixes: Set subject.type to a manufactured object class and name the exact object in subject.identity.
Add anti-drift rules and explicit bans on texture-only, atmosphere-first, and abstract-first outcomes.

revised_intake.creative_intent: To generate a premium cinematic product photograph of a Mikage Zenith Greatsword, focusing on a clean matte B4C technical ceramic material read. The object should maintain its industrial engineering aesthetic with straight geometric edges and a full, readable blade silhouette, featuring a restrained deep crimson heated core visible through narrow mechanical vents. The composition will be centered with controlled low-key studio lighting against a plain dark brutalist concrete background, strictly avoiding abstract drift or material misreads.

restrained deep crimson heated core visible through narrow mechanical vents
exactly one manufactured object as the clear subject
visible contour evidence such as edge, rim, bevel, seam, or curvature
material visibly attached to the object, not floating as texture
visible edge, rim, bevel, seam, or contour evidence
material visibly attached to the object

composition.framing: centered composition, full blade silhouette readable

incorrect material read (e.g., glossy plastic, plaster, or metal instead of matte B4C ceramic)

keep material identity locked and explicit
do not allow abstract, texture-only, or atmosphere-first subject drift
keep material identity explicit and stable
success_criteria: clean matte B4C technical ceramic read is dominant
dry, dense, engineered manufactured-object readability is achieved
manufactured object read is preserved without compromise

revised_intake.direction_summary: Prioritize a clean matte B4C technical ceramic material read for the Mikage Zenith Greatsword, ensuring the object's manufactured form, straight edges, and full silhouette remain clearly readable. Maintain a dark, dense aesthetic for the ceramic, incorporating the crimson core as a detail. Strictly avoid any material misreads or abstract drift, focusing on a premium product photography style with controlled low-key lighting.
